title: Diamond Challenge
description: Global high school entrepreneurship competition run by Horn Entrepreneurship at the University of Delaware, open to teams worldwide since 2012. Teams of 2-4 students (ages 14-18 at the submission deadline) plus one required adult advisor (21+) compete in a Business Innovation or Social Innovation track: a written concept narrative plus 60-second video, submission-round judging, and a live or virtual pitching round, with top teams advancing to the Limitless World Summit finals on UD's campus. Free to enter; has reached more than 18,000 students from 120+ countries historically. Grand prizes per track: $12,000 (1st), $8,000 (2nd), $4,500 (3rd), plus additional topical prizes.
selectivity_evidence: Official competition page states teams advance through submission-round judging and pitching rounds based on 'the most promising ideas'; a limited set of grand-prize and topical-prize winners is selected out of a global applicant pool that has historically reached 18,000+ students from 120+ countries. No numeric acceptance rate is published.

title: John Locke Institute Global Essay Prize
description: International argumentative essay competition run by the Oxford-based John Locke Institute, open worldwide to students under 19 as of the submission deadline with no minimum age. Entrants write a single essay (up to 2,000 words) answering one question from ten subject categories: Economics, History, International Relations, Law, Philosophy, Politics, Psychology, Public Policy, Science & Technology, and Theology. Essays are assessed by senior academics from leading universities on knowledge, evidence quality, argumentation, originality, structure, and persuasive force; senior and junior entrants are judged separately within each category. Free to enter (late-submission extensions cost £25-75). Prizes per category: $5,000 (1st), $2,000 (2nd), $1,000 (3rd) scholarships, plus a $10,000 honorary fellowship for the best overall essay across all categories.
selectivity_evidence: Essays are assessed by senior academics from leading universities on knowledge, evidence, argumentation, originality, structure, and persuasive force, with only a 1st/2nd/3rd winner named per category and a single overall Grand Prize; the official page does not publish a numeric entrant count or win rate.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle (concluded; regular deadline was May 31, 2026); 2027 cycle dates not yet posted at verification
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly on 2026-08-20.

title: National Economics Challenge
description: America's premier high school economics competition, run by the Council for Economic Education. Teams of three to four students, coached by a teacher, take a 30-question online exam within a 35-minute time limit covering micro- and macroeconomic principles and the world economy; close to 10,000 students compete annually, advancing from state-level competition to the National Finals. Two divisions: the Adam Smith Division for students enrolled in AP/IB/honors economics or returning competitors, and the David Ricardo Division for first-time competitors who have completed no more than one economics course. National Finals prizes: $1,000 (1st), $500 (2nd), $250 (3rd), $200 (4th), plus an all-expenses-paid trip (excluding travel) for finalist teams. The 2026 National Finals were held in Atlanta, GA, May 28-29, 2026, following a state-registration window of January 1-April 8, 2026 via the econchallenge.unl.edu portal.
selectivity_evidence: State-level competitions narrow close to 10,000 annual participants down to a small set of National Finalist teams; the two-division structure (Adam Smith for advanced/returning competitors, David Ricardo for first-timers) segments difficulty rather than gating entry. The official page does not publish a numeric national win rate.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle (concluded May 28-29, 2026); 2027 cycle dates not yet posted at verification
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly on 2026-08-20.

title: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
description: Long-running national creative-arts competition for teens in grades 7-12, aged 13 and up, residing in the United States, U.S. territories/military bases, or Canada (excluding Quebec) - including homeschooled students and American schools operating abroad. Students submit original work through a regional affiliate in more than 20 categories of art and writing; a separate Portfolio category (eight pieces sharing a cohesive vision) is open only to graduating seniors. Entry fees are $15 per individual entry and $40 per portfolio, with fee waivers available without requiring proof of financial need. Entries open each fall, with deadlines set regionally beginning in December. National Medalists are eligible for scholarships of up to $12,500.
residency_restrictions: Must reside in the United States, U.S. territories, or U.S. military bases, or Canada (excluding Quebec); American schools operating abroad are also eligible.
application_requirements: portfolio or individual work upload via regional affiliate

title: DECA Competitive Events Program (International Career Development Conference)
description: DECA prepares high school students for careers in marketing, finance, hospitality, and management through a membership-based Competitive Events program spanning nearly 60 role-play, prepared, and online events across six career pathways: Business Management & Administration, Entrepreneurship, Finance, Hospitality & Tourism, Marketing, and Personal Financial Literacy. Students compete through their school's chartered DECA chapter, advancing from chapter-level events to regional/state conferences and, for top performers, to the International Career Development Conference (ICDC), which gathers more than 25,000 high school students, teacher-advisors, business professionals, and alumni annually. Winners can earn scholarships, recognition, and travel opportunities. The 2027 ICDC will be held April 17-20 in Anaheim, CA.
residency_restrictions: Participation requires membership through an official school DECA chapter on a DECA roster; the high-school program page reviewed does not state whether non-U.S. schools may charter a chapter.
application_requirements: membership through a chartered school DECA chapter

title: Science Olympiad (Division C)
description: The leading U.S. team STEM competition for grades 9-12 (Division C), run by the nonprofit Science Olympiad since 1984. High school teams of up to 15 students (no more than seven twelfth-graders), all from the same school under the same administrator, compete across dozens of biology, chemistry, physics, earth-science, and engineering events, in pairs or trios per event. Teams register through their state chapter and progress from regional invitationals to state tournaments, with top state teams advancing to the National Tournament (the 2026 National Tournament was held at USC). Over 7,000 teams compete at 450+ tournaments across all 50 states annually. The 43rd season's rules are released September 8, 2026.
residency_restrictions: Teams must be composed entirely of students from a single school under a single administrator, recruited through the school's state chapter; the official homepage does not describe an international participation pathway.
selectivity_evidence: Advancement runs through regional invitational, state tournament, and national tournament rounds; the official homepage does not publish acceptance or advancement-rate figures.

title: FIRST Robotics Competition
organization: FIRST (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology)
description: International high school robotics competition for grades 9-12 (ages 14-18). Each January, teams of roughly 10-25 students, guided by adult mentors, receive a Kit of Parts and about six weeks to design, program, and build an industrial-sized robot for that season's game, then compete on themed fields as part of shifting three-team alliances at regional and championship events. Teams also handle fundraising, community STEM outreach, and building a team brand/identity. The 2024-25 season drew approximately 93,000 students on teams from 35 countries. The next season (FIRST CANOPY, including the BIOCORE challenge) releases January 9, 2027.
application_requirements: Youth Registration & Consent Form (parent/guardian signature required if under 18)
selectivity_evidence: Entry is open to any registered team with a school/organization affiliation and adult mentor (no competitive application gate to join); competitive selection occurs through regional and championship event results rather than at entry, so no admissions-style tier applies.
current_cycle_label: FIRST CANOPY season, kicks off January 9, 2027

title: European Union Contest for Young Scientists (EUCYS)
organization: European Commission (Directorate-General for Research and Innovation)
description: Pan-European science competition for young scientists aged 14-20, run under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme to highlight top European student research and encourage careers in science and innovation. Entry is not direct: competitors must be first-prize-winning individuals or teams (up to 3 participants) from their own country's national science contest; each of the roughly 40 participating countries (EU members, Associated Countries, and Neighbourhood Countries) may submit up to 3 projects. At the contest, participants present a video, written project, and exhibition poster, and answer questions from a scientific jury. EUCYS 2026 takes place September 22-27 in Kiel, Germany, bringing together approximately 150 young scientists. Prizes include four first-place awards of EUR7,000 each, four second-place awards of EUR5,000, four third-place awards of EUR3,500, a EUR2,500 Special Jury Prize, plus study-visit prizes to leading scientific organizations.
residency_restrictions: Entry requires having already won first prize at one's own country's national science contest; direct individual entry to EUCYS is not possible.
application_requirements: prior first-prize win at a national science contest
selectivity_evidence: Only first-prize winners of each participating country's own national contest may compete, and each of the roughly 40 eligible countries may send at most 3 projects (up to 6 contestants), producing a final field of about 150 young scientists Europe-wide.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly on 2026-08-20.

title: UK Chemistry Olympiad
description: National chemistry competition open to secondary school and college students across the British Isles, recommended for students aged 16+ in their last year of study before higher education (younger students may enter if confident in the material). Schools and colleges register students centrally - there is no individual application route. Round One is a two-hour written exam covering real-world chemistry problems, sat in person under school supervision; roughly 25-30 students advance to Round Two and potential UK training/selection for the International Chemistry Olympiad team. Free for schools throughout the British Isles; certain British international schools in Asia (China, Hong Kong, Japan, Malaysia, Mongolia, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam) may also enter via a partner organization for a fee, and other British-curriculum international schools may contact the RSC about eligibility. Registration for the next round opens September 16, 2026.
residency_restrictions: Free entry is limited to schools/colleges in the British Isles; British-curriculum international schools may enter only via a listed partner route or by separately confirming eligibility with the RSC.
selectivity_evidence: Round One is open to any registered school's students with no prior qualifying step, but only about 25-30 students nationally advance from Round One to Round Two, from which the UK's 4-student International Chemistry Olympiad team is eventually selected.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly on 2026-08-20.

title: HOSA Future Health Professionals - Competitive Events
description: International student organization recognized by the U.S. Department of Education, focused on health-science and biomedical career pathways, with a secondary (high school) division alongside postsecondary, adult, and collegiate divisions. Members join through a locally chartered HOSA chapter (affiliation is arranged by the chapter's advisor, who obtains a charter number and password from HOSA Headquarters or the State Advisor) and compete in structured Competitive Events across health-science, health-professions, emergency-preparedness, leadership, and teamwork categories, progressing from the local chapter through regional and state competition to the International Leadership Conference (ILC). The organization has grown to over 200,000 members through 51 chartered HOSA Associations, including chapters in American Samoa, Canada, Germany, Italy, and Puerto Rico in addition to U.S. states.

title: American Regions Mathematics League (ARML)
description: Annual team mathematics competition in which teams representing a geographic region (state, metro area, or country) compete simultaneously at multiple host-university sites. Every student competes as part of a regional team of high-school age or younger (ARML is not an open individual signup - students join through their region's qualifying math team, with regional qualifying processes varying by area). The 2026 competition was held May 31, 2026, at five U.S. university sites (Penn State University, University of Nevada-Reno, University of Iowa, Western Carolina University, and St. Anselm College), drawing 128 teams and over 1,800 students from the United States, Canada, China, and South Korea.

title: Journal of Emerging Investigators (JEI)
description: Peer-reviewed, open-access science journal, run by Harvard graduate students, that publishes original hypothesis-driven research (social, physical, or biological sciences) by middle- and high-school students aged 13 and older, up until they enroll in university. A senior adult author (teacher, professor, postdoc, senior graduate student, or - for home research - a parent) must be listed as final author and is required to submit the manuscript on the student's behalf; students may not submit their own work. JEI charges a single $49 fee at the time of submission that covers both review and eventual publication, with no separate publication fee; fee waivers are available for authors in financial need. Submissions are accepted on a rolling basis (no fixed deadline), and review timelines vary based on submission volume and revision completeness.
selectivity_evidence: Manuscripts go through a formal peer-review process with editors and reviewers before a publication decision; not every submission is accepted, though the official pages fetched do not publish a numeric acceptance rate.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly on 2026-08-20.

title: Rise
organization: Schmidt Futures and the Rhodes Trust
description: Global talent programme, launched by Schmidt Futures in partnership with the Rhodes Trust, that identifies promising young people ages 15-17 from around the world and supports them for life. Applicants complete the multi-stage 'Rise Challenge' (introductory videos, an individual project demonstrating talent and community benefit, and peer review of other applicants' projects) through the Hello World Network mobile app, with web-browser and paper alternatives for applicants without mobile access; up to 500 Finalists advance to interactive 'Finalist Days' interviews. Each year Rise selects 100 Global Winners, who receive a four-year need-based post-secondary scholarship (tuition and living stipend), a fully funded multi-week residential summit with the winner cohort, mentorship and career services, a technology starter package, and lifetime access to further funding and graduate-scholarship opportunities. The inaugural cohort was chosen from tens of thousands of applicants across 42 countries; the program states it now draws applicants from more than 170 countries.

Finalist Days interview (if selected as a Finalist)
selectivity_evidence: The programme's own announcement of its first cohort states 100 Global Winners were selected 'from tens of thousands of applicants' representing 42 countries in that cycle, with up to 500 Finalists advancing to in-person interviews before final selection.

title: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
description: National scholarship recognizing exceptional, largely independent work by students 18 or younger, open to U.S. citizens residing in the U.S., U.S. permanent residents, or students on active-duty U.S. military status stationed overseas (no minimum age). Applicants submit a significant completed project in one of three categories - STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics), Humanities (Music, Literature, Philosophy), or Outside the Box (graduate-level work completed under expert supervision); visual/performing-arts-only projects such as photography, sculpture, or film are not eligible. Two-person teams may apply if both members individually meet all eligibility criteria, with scholarship funds split evenly. Applications require two non-family nominators, category-specific supporting materials, and a commitment from the applicant and a parent to attend an in-person awards reception in Washington, D.C. Awards are given at three levels: $100,000, $50,000, and $25,000 (split evenly for team entries). The 2026 application deadline was February 18, 2026; the 2027 cycle opens in fall 2026 with its deadline not yet posted.
citizenship_restrictions: U.S. citizens residing in the U.S., U.S. permanent residents, or active-duty U.S. military stationed overseas.

title: Türkiye Scholarships - Bachelor's Degree Programme
organization: Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB), Government of Turkiye
description: Government-of-Turkiye international scholarship program, running since 1992, that funds international students to study associate or bachelor's degrees at Turkish universities.
